Measurements: 12 shapes x GC/1.2.5 -O4 (12/12 agree with the rule, zero counterexamples); 17 optimization/pragma settings on the init_attract_mode shape (0/17 emit a table); 29 archive compilers at -O4 on that shape (0/29 emit a table). The retail target's own table, jumptable_8011892C, is 10 entries resolving to 5 distinct addresses (+0x14C, +0x180 x2, +0x1D0 x5 = the default, +0x1B0, +0x16C), which is BELOW this threshold -- so the retail attract.c was built by a toolchain outside the local archive, and the law's practical use here is that it CLOSES the axis rather than opening it.

falsifier: Exhibit any C switch that compiles under an archive MWCC to a bctr jump table while having five or fewer distinct branch destinations (default counted once when in-range reachable), or a compare chain while having six or more. Run `python tools/gdl/composed_census/at_switch_emission_threshold.py --phases 1`: it prints DESTS, the observed emission and the rule's prediction per shape, and flags any row as MISFIT. A single MISFIT row disproves the law. The counting rule for `destinations` is the falsifiable part: count the distinct code addresses the switch can transfer to, adding the default once iff some value in [min,max] falls through to it.
subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: MWCC emits a switch JUMP TABLE (slwi/lwzx/mtctr/bctr behind a cmplwi+bgt range guard) if and only if the switch has at least SIX DISTINCT BRANCH DESTINATIONS, counting the default exactly once when it is reachable from inside [min_case,max_case]. Below six it emits a compare chain. Three things that are widely assumed to be the knob are MEASURED NOT TO BE: (a) CASE COUNT and LABEL COUNT -- a switch whose ten labels 0..9 resolve to five destinations gets a chain, while one whose six labels resolve to six destinations gets a table; (b) RANGE and DENSITY -- shape S12 spreads the same five destinations over the range 0..20 and still gets a chain, so density is not consulted at all; (c) EMPTY-CASE SPELLING -- empty case bodies merge into the default BEFORE the decision is taken, and the merge is complete: writing 3/5/6/7/8 as five separate `case N: break;` groups (S8) produces an object BYTE-IDENTICAL to writing them as one five-label group (S1), 1384 bytes both ways. Distinct destinations, not distinct bodies, is the count: S9 gives two case groups textually IDENTICAL bodies and still scores six, because MWCC does not tail-merge non-empty case blocks before deciding. Corollary for reconstruction: when a target emits a table that our build renders as a chain, the case SET is not the lever and no rewriting of case labels, case order, `default:` placement, cast signedness, or empty-group spelling will reach it -- 12 of 12 shapes and 17 of 17 flag settings confirm. See claim.law.IT_empty-bodied-if-elides-its-own-comparison for the analogous elision on `if`.
